title: Insulin action times

findings.where: All images: chart vertical axis; insulin.jsx STYLE.h
findings.title: Curve heights imply an unsupported strength comparison
findings.problem: The shared vertical axis and gridlines show rapid insulin almost three times taller than glargine, using arbitrary heights of 112 versus 40. Nothing explains that these heights cannot establish comparative potency or glucose-lowering effect. Calling the curves illustrative does not explicitly resolve that implication.
findings.fix: State that heights are schematic and not a comparison of dose or potency, or place independently normalized profiles in separate lanes. Label the horizontal axis 'Hours after dose' as well.

findings.where: Images 3 and 11, step rapid: Meal annotation
findings.title: Meal icon sits beyond the rapid insulin's duration
findings.problem: The plate is positioned at hx(6.6), after the drawn insulin effect ends at 5 hours. Its curved leader returns to dose time, but its position within a timed plot can still read as eating several hours after injection rather than as an untimed callout.
findings.fix: Move the plate above the dose-time origin or outside the plotting area, with an unambiguous leader. Retain the product-specific timing caveat.

findings.where: Images 8 and 16, step worked: highlighted NPH path
findings.title: Thickening the NPH stroke closes its dotted gaps
findings.problem: The worked stroke is 4 units wide but retains dasharray '2 4' with round caps. Those caps consume the entire 4-unit gap, making adjacent dots touch. The highlight therefore looks substantially more continuous than the dotted NPH legend and ordinary NPH curve.
findings.fix: Keep the original stroke width and add emphasis behind it, or increase the highlighted dash gaps so the dotted identity remains visibly separated at phone width.

assessment: No clear clinical blocker in the stated typical ranges or overnight peak-window arithmetic. Three visual teaching ambiguities remain.
